question: Ten people in a café earn £30,000 a year; an eleventh earns £1.1 million. What is the mean income, in thousands of pounds?
answer: About 127.3 thousand pounds, while the median is still £30,000.
move: When one value is huge, ask for the middle, not the mean.
ask: When I compare myself with an average, do I know whether a few extremes are pulling it up?
trap: Expecting the average to describe a typical person in the room.
hint: Add up all eleven incomes, then divide by eleven.
steps: About 127.3 thousand pounds, while the median is still £30,000.
source: Huff, How to Lie with Statistics, 1954
reference: Huff, How to Lie with Statistics, W. W. Norton, 1954
